### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c34a5ce3a7e4ddd62e1833dfd34fd7f7fa179296` — the merge of head `0fb1c3aa9811a6a3fc102b851faa9728a5eef23e` into base `a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c34a5ce3a7e4ddd62e1833dfd34fd7f7fa179296 && git checkout c34a5ce3a7e4ddd62e1833dfd34fd7f7fa179296
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff 0fb1c3aa9811a6a3fc102b851faa9728a5eef23e && git checkout -B drift-repro a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff && git merge --no-ff 0fb1c3aa9811a6a3fc102b851faa9728a5eef23e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6001927ad3e16daaf51160b9fcc07e57fbff36c7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-refusal-envelope.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dotted-dimension-unbacked-join-parity.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts + packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-refusal.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/hop-object.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx, packages/rest/src/analytics-relationship-path-admission.test.ts, objectui packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts (all read at origin/main 50646f01f2, objectui origin/main)

### ① Derived judgments

Read from the diff and the live tree, each accept-set or public-surface change the hunks imply:

1. **`queryDataset`, native strategy: a selected dimension through an undeclared relationship path moves from `DATASET_INVALID` / 400 to `INVALID_FIELD` / 400.** Right. On main the only thing refusing it is `NativeSQLStrategy.assembleStatement`'s join allowlist (native-sql-strategy.ts:1497–1526), which reads `ctx.getAllowedRelationships(cube)`; `cubeReads` answers that from `scope.getCompiledDataset(name)?.allowedRelationships` (analytics-service.ts:1759–1762). The new `assertDimensionJoinsBacked` reads the identical set from the identical scope, so what it refuses is exactly the subset of allowlist refusals that come from a `dimensions` entry, and nothing the allowlist accepted becomes refused. The status is unchanged; only the code and the envelope (`member`, `param: 'dimensions'`, `cube` via `invalidMemberError`, dataset-refusal.ts:183) change. The ruling on the card (claim 6553559505, agreeing with triage 6532297703) asked for exactly this.

2. **`queryDataset`, ObjectQL strategy: a real lookup the dataset does not include (`account.name`, no `include`) was served and is now refused.** Right, and it is a narrowing the card's wording covers. `ObjectQLStrategy` has no allowlist read at all (grep for `getAllowedRelationships` / `allowedRelationships` in objectql-strategy.ts returns nothing); its `lookupMember` (objectql-strategy.ts:1662–1683) mints the same synthetic `{ sql: member }` the native strategy does and `planCrossObject` then FK-expands it. The spec's own `include` doc says "D-C: only declared paths are joinable" (dataset.zod.ts:643–648), and the published docs page says "Only declared paths are joinable" (analytics.mdx:248). Serving it was the ObjectQL face failing the spec's refusal; refusing it makes the refusal real.

3. **Draft preview (`previewDrafts: true`): the one `null` group is now the same refusal.** Right. `evaluateAnalyticsQueryOverRows` (preview-evaluator.ts:860–866) reads `r[String(dim?.sql ?? name)]`, so an undotted-in-the-row member like `account.name` reads `undefined` and every row lands under `null`. The gate is asked at the same point in the preview's gate list as in `callCtx` (after `assertNoInternalFieldsQueried` and `assertFieldsReadable`), reading `compiled.allowedRelationships` directly, so the message is byte-equal by construction (one method, no copy).

4. **The gate sits in `callCtx`, which `queryIn` (both `query()` and `queryDataset`'s executor) and `generateSql()` share.** Right as placement: it inherits the #20933 order (object exposure, read admission, stored-body, internal-field, field-level, then this gate, then the order-key door at the same seam). It means the narrowing also reaches `/analytics/query` and `/analytics/sql` for a cube that is a *registered* dataset (`sharedScope.getCompiledDataset` answers from `datasetRegistry`, analytics-service.ts:1492, 2620). Native already refused there (allowlist); ObjectQL served there and now refuses. Same compiled dataset, same accept set, same gate, so it is the same narrowing, but see ② for the prose.

5. **Hand-authored cubes (no compiled dataset), `timeDimensions`, `where`/`runtimeFilter` members, expression `sql`, and dotted spellings that resolve to a declared dimension are untouched.** Right. `allowed` is `undefined` for a non-dataset cube so the gate returns; the loop reads `query.dimensions` only; `declaredMemberEntry` (analytics-service.ts:377–405) is the exact mirror of the strategies' `lookupMember` chain (`bag[member]`, `<cube>.<tail>`, `bag[tail]`, flattened), so `<cube>.region` and `<object>.region` skip the gate as both strategies would resolve them; `IDENTIFIER_PATH` (line 434) is the same regex `qualifyAndRegisterJoin` tests before splitting a path, so an expression is passed through as the strategy passes it.

6. **`unbackedRelationshipPath` (new export of dataset-compiler.ts) is not a public-surface change.** Right. `src/index.ts` re-exports `compileDataset` and five types from `dataset-compiler.js` by name (lines 15–22); nothing is re-exported wholesale, so the package's published surface is unchanged. Its hop-by-hop walk uses the same `joinAlias` (`.`→`__`) the compiler registers joins under and `resolvePathHops` builds aliases with (hop-object.ts:81), and `allowedRelationships` holds every prefix (dataset-compiler.ts:769), so a fully declared multi-hop path answers `null` and `account.owner.name` over `include: ['account']` answers `account.owner`. Correct.

7. **The rest refusal-envelope row's trigger moves from a dotted `dimensions` entry to a `runtimeFilter` member.** Right. The old trigger is this card's case and is now refused ahead of the strategy; a `runtimeFilter` member reaches `resolveFieldSql` → `qualifyAndRegisterJoin` → the allowlist, which the allowlist's own comment names as a caller-shaped trigger (native-sql-strategy.ts:1505–1510). The `listEntry` audit trail and the message regex are kept, so the #5367 coverage that row exists for still holds.

8. **No `DATASET_INVALID` consumer is broken by the code change.** Verified, not taken from the report. objectui `packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts` ~6989–7020: `PERMISSION_DENIED` is typed (③), a code-less answer is read by status (④), and every other named code, `DATASET_INVALID` and `INVALID_FIELD` alike, falls to branch ⑤'s generic `Error('Dataset query failed: …')`. Its two `DATASET_INVALID` test files use the code as fixture text. HotCRM has no reader; `packages/client`, `apps`, `examples`, `skills` and `content/docs` name `DATASET_INVALID` only for compile-time (dataset-definition) refusals, never for a selection-side dotted dimension. The triage condition "if the review finds the code has consumers, it comes back as a decision card" is not met.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28258-dotted-dimension-unbacked-join.md`: `'@objectstack/service-analytics': patch`, with a **BREAKING** banner, the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` lines at line start, an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and a remedy line. That matches the diff: nothing authorable changes (no spec key, no export, no config field), so under AGENTS.md's level rule ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition") `patch` is the correct level, and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong because `@objectstack/service-analytics` publishes. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines at line start; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm (two faces stop serving, one face changes code; nothing is widened: both codes were already on the wire, no answer member is added). `Check Changeset` on the head is `success`.

One precision point, should-fix, prose only: the `Clause-②` sentence in both the PR body and the changeset names "a `queryDataset` selection". The gate is in `callCtx`, so the same narrowing is live on `/analytics/query` and `/analytics/sql` whenever `cube` names a registered dataset (judgment ① 4). The PR body's "What changes" says so ("shared by `query()` and `generateSql()`"); the declaration line and the changeset's "Who sees it" do not. Naming the two doors there would make the ledger entry complete. It is the same accept set, so this is wording, not a missing narrowing.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Check-runs on `6001927ad`** (`filter=latest`, 50 runs): 16 `success` (including Check Changeset, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Type Check · source gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Plan Test Core shards), 17 `skipped` (UI and opt-in lanes, correctly, for a server-only diff), 0 failures, and **17 still `in_progress` at review time**: Build Core, Test Core 1/8–8/8, Type Check · consumer gates / debt ledger / workspace, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI, and a second Check Changeset instance. This record judges on the code; the seat reads those conclusions before landing. The dev's own runs on the code head (`9b932230a`, which `6001927ad` differs from only in changeset prose) report service-analytics 201 files / 4823 tests green, rest `src/analytics` 23 files green, typecheck 0, 62/62 derived gate families exit 0, and the full dogfood battery 2932 passed / 0 failed; nothing in the diff contradicts those readings.

**`open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer or escalate.

**Dev flags in the os-dev-report (6554100004) and the PR's Acceptance notes:**

- *Native code change measured for consumers first.* Done correctly; I re-measured it (① 8). No real consumer, so both halves land, as the claim allowed.
- *ObjectQL face narrows too (served `account.name`).* Within the ruling: the card's contract is "a dimension spelled through a join the dataset does not back", which a real lookup outside `include` is. Pinned in the new test on real SQLite. Right.
- *First cut in `ensureCube` broke #20933's 403 and was moved to `callCtx`.* The right placement. `analytics-relationship-path-admission.test.ts:372–377` pins that an undeclared path to an unreadable related object answers 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and `queryObjects` (analytics-service.ts, via `namedQueryFields` → `resolvePathHops` → the field's `reference`) admits the hop's object before this gate runs. The order-key door sits on the same seam for the same reason.
- *Preview vs a denied related object (not measured).* The preview admits `cubeObjects` only (base object and declared joins), so an undeclared path through an unreadable object would answer the field gate's verdict then this gate's 400 where the live faces answer 403. That is a pre-existing property of the preview (it reads no related object), not something this diff introduces or worsens: before, the same request served a `null` group. It is honestly declared; it does not block.
- *Rest test row moved.* Right (① 7).
- *Card assignee untouched, PR without labels at open.* Fine; the labels now on the PR are bot-applied.
- *`timeDimensions` left alone on the claim both live faces already answer `INVALID_FIELD`.* Not changed by this diff, so not a gate here; recorded as out-of-scope finding 2.

**The four out-of-scope findings (class a) and the fifth unmeasured note — does any block this PR?** No.
1. *Preview serves a `null` group for a BACKED dotted dimension and for `OBJECT.region`/`CUBE.region`.* This is the "declared capability not delivered" case: the spec declares a declared path joinable, the preview joins nothing. The PR does the right thing with it: it does **not** refuse it (the two CONTROL tests assert the preview is not refused for `account.name` with `include: ['account']` and for `os28258_deal.region`), leaving it an implementation gap for its own card. Not blocking.
2. *Dotted `timeDimensions` on the preview drops the time dimension.* Different member position, same family; its own card.
3. *`runtimeFilter` through an undeclared path: native `DATASET_INVALID`, ObjectQL `INVALID_FIELD`, preview `[]`.* The same three-answer split in the filter position. The ruling scoped this card to the dimension, and the native allowlist's `DATASET_INVALID` for this position is explicitly kept by the claim ("`DATASET_INVALID` stays for every other reason it is raised"). Its own card.
4. *Declared path to a column the related object lacks: native 500.* A separate defect on the native face; its own card.
5. *Preview vs denied related object* (covered above). Not blocking.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged over the four code paths against the spec on `main`. The question is whether the narrowing takes a declared capability away at the consumer, or makes the spec's own refusal real.

It makes the refusal real. `DatasetSchema.include` is documented as the one source of joinable paths ("D-C: only declared paths are joinable; no arbitrary predicates", dataset.zod.ts:647–648); `compileDataset`'s header says the same of the compiler ("every dotted field reference must point at a relationship that the dataset explicitly declared in `include`; otherwise the compile fails", dataset-compiler.ts:35–39) and the returned `allowedRelationships` is described as "the join allowlist the strategy enforces at SQL-build time". On `main` that allowlist is enforced by one strategy out of three; the ObjectQL strategy and the preview silently served what the spec says is refused. The PR moves the judgment one layer up, to the seam all three faces share, and reads the same set. No consumer loses anything the spec grants: a declared path serves as before (CONTROL pins on both live strategies, same groups), a dotted spelling that resolves to a declared dimension serves as before, and a hand-authored cube is unaffected.

I tried to break it:

- *Could the gate refuse something the allowlist accepts?* No: it reads the same `Set` the allowlist reads, through the same scope, with the same alias convention and the prefix closure already in the set.
- *Could it pre-empt an earlier verdict?* Only verdicts the ruling wanted after it: it runs after the object, stored-body, internal-field and field-level gates, so an unreadable related object still answers 403, and the `nope` measure CONTROL shows a measure mistake is still answered first on every face (`ensureCube`'s order).
- *Does it diverge from the strategies' member resolution?* No: `declaredMemberEntry` is the documented mirror of both `lookupMember`s and was already the gate-side resolver for #5520/#5669; `IDENTIFIER_PATH` is the strategy's own path test.
- *Is the `<cube>.bogus` spelling handled?* Yes, consistently with both strategies: `declaredMemberEntry` finds no `bogus`, the member is a path, hop `<cube>` is not an alias, so it is refused `INVALID_FIELD` naming the member. Before, native refused it as a join (`DATASET_INVALID`) for the same reason. The one soft spot is the message: for `<cube>.bogus` (and the card's own `<object>.bogus`) it says the member "traverses relationship path '<cube>'", which is what both strategies would have done with it but not what the author meant. The "Valid dimensions: …" tail carries the remedy, so this is a **should-fix** on wording (a clause such as "no such relationship or dimension" would name the mistake either way), not a correctness issue.
- *Does the preview's gate read a different cube from the live faces?* It reads `compiled.cube` with minted measures spread in, the same cube the preview's other gates read; dimensions are not minted, so the result is the same as the live faces' post-`ensureCube` cube for this question.
- *Is anything widened?* No. No new code, status, export, or answer member; the `member`/`param`/`cube` fields are the ones every other `invalidMemberError` already carries.

Findings: no must-fix. Should-fix (1): name the `/analytics/query` and `/analytics/sql` doors over a registered dataset in the `Clause-②` sentence and the changeset's "Who sees it" (② above). Should-fix (2): the refusal message's "traverses relationship path" clause for a `<cube>.`/`<object>.` qualified spelling (④ above). Both are prose; neither changes what the gate accepts or refuses.
